editions.text: Yesterday marked the busiest day in the past week, with 268 feeder visits and 21 species recorded, well above the seven-day average of 97 visits and 12 species. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees were the dominant visual presences, maintaining their status as regulars present every day this week. The station’s new seed feeder and treat bowl, installed over the past week, coincided with a significant increase in visitor diversity and frequency. A Black-capped Chickadee provided the station’s first confident visual record, joining a list that included a Common Gallinule, also a first visual for this location. The day closed with a final auditory detection of a Ruby-throated Hummingbird at 20:30. The high volume of detections, particularly from Carolina Wrens and Northern Cardinals, reflects the continued presence of the new microphone installed on September 13.

Tufted Titmice began visiting the feeder at 07:10, six minutes before sunrise. By the time the light fully came in, their chatter had joined the early calls of Northern Cardinals and Carolina Wrens. The station has logged 132 visits, significantly busier than the recent daily average of 90 at this hour.

Ruby-throated Hummingbirds arrived in force at 08:00, accounting for 44 detections in that hour alone. They were soon joined by a rush of Carolina Chickadees and Blue Jays, creating a dense mix of voices that continued through the 09:00 hour. Twenty-two species are recorded so far, nearly double the usual count for this time of morning.

Midday brought a shift in activity as the Ruby-throated Hummingbirds eased off and the Blue Jays took over the acoustic space, recording 19 detections in the 14:00 hour alone. Eastern Towhees were heard consistently through the afternoon, with a peak of 18 detections during the 13:00 hour.

The Tufted Titmice remains the most frequent visual presence with 74 confident visits, followed by Carolina Chickadees at 34. A single Northern Flicker was recorded as a probable sighting. The weather is holding steady with a high of 28.2°C, light wind, and no precipitation.
